title: Markets: Tesla, Meta, Barclays, Norway’s fund and oil risks
summary: Today’s edition covers Tesla earnings, Meta’s New Mexico judgment, SpaceX results, Barclays’ job cuts, Norway’s wealth-fund loss and rising oil prices amid Strait of Hormuz reports.

stories.headline: Tesla beats on earnings and sales even as auto revenue declines
stories.dek: Tesla reported third-quarter results as its vehicle revenue fell, while the company also faces questions about a possible SpaceX combination.
tldr: Tesla reported third-quarter net income of $787 million, down 44% year over year, while revenue was roughly flat at $28 billion.
Adjusted earnings per share of 48 cents exceeded analyst expectations, even as revenue fell slightly short of forecasts, according to the Associated Press.
Elon Musk said special committees at Tesla and SpaceX were considering a possible combination, but both companies still face hurdles and no deal has been announced.

body.text: Tesla reported third-quarter net income of $787 million, or 22 cents per share, down 44% from the year-earlier period, the Associated Press reported. Revenue was approximately $28 billion and broadly flat, slightly below analyst forecasts.

Adjusted earnings per share were 48 cents, beating analysts’ expectations by 3 cents, according to AP. CNBC reported that Tesla beat on earnings and sales even as automotive revenue declined, highlighting mixed performance across the business.

The results arrived as Elon Musk said special committees at Tesla and SpaceX had been set up to discuss a possible combination. Musk cautioned that significant hurdles remained, and the companies had not announced an agreement.

Tesla shares moved higher after the results in after-hours trading, AP reported. The filings and earnings call provide the confirmed quarter results; the timing, structure and feasibility of any Tesla-SpaceX transaction remain unresolved.

stories.whyItMatters: Tesla’s results combine a reported earnings beat with weaker automotive revenue, so headline earnings alone do not describe the operating picture. A potential combination with SpaceX adds a separate governance and capital-allocation question, but remains exploratory.
stories.editorNote: Quarter figures are attributed to company reporting and AP/CNBC coverage; the possible combination is not a completed transaction.

stories.headline: Meta ordered to pay New Mexico $25 billion for deceiving users about privacy on Facebook
stories.dek: A judge set the penalty after a jury found Meta liable in a case tied to Facebook user privacy; Meta said it would appeal.
tldr: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion after a jury found the company misled users about privacy on Facebook.
The case followed allegations that Cambridge Analytica obtained personal data from millions of Facebook users without consent.
Meta said it would appeal, so the amount and timing of any payment remain subject to further court proceedings.

body.text: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta Platforms to pay $25 billion after a jury found the company had misled consumers about Facebook privacy, Reuters and the Associated Press reported. The judgment followed a state lawsuit first filed in 2021.

The case arose from allegations that Cambridge Analytica obtained Facebook users’ personal data through a third-party app without their consent. New Mexico accused Meta of misrepresenting data access and the platform’s handling of harmful content and misinformation.

The state’s law allows penalties of up to $5,000 per violation, with proceeds directed to New Mexico’s school system, according to Reuters. The $25 billion award reflects the judge’s ruling on the jury’s findings, rather than a settled payment.
Meta said it disagreed with the ruling and planned to appeal. The appeal could take years and may alter the amount or liability findings, so the ultimate payment and timing remain unsettled.

stories.whyItMatters: The judgment makes privacy-related legal exposure financially material for a large platform, while the appeal means the award is not yet a final cash outflow. The case also revives scrutiny of how platforms describe data practices after third-party access.
stories.editorNote: The judgment is reported by AP and Reuters; the penalty remains subject to Meta’s announced appeal.

stories.headline: Elon Musk's SpaceX reports a profit and he hints at a possible merger with Tesla
stories.dek: SpaceX reported a $4.4 billion quarterly profit as its AI business grew, while directors began considering a possible Tesla combination.
tldr: SpaceX reported a $4.4 billion profit and $14.6 billion in revenue for the quarter through September, according to the Associated Press.
Elon Musk said independent committees at SpaceX and Tesla had been formed to discuss a possible combination, while describing a deal as uncertain.
SpaceX said capital expenditure reached $19.6 billion last quarter and forecast $35 billion to $40 billion for the current quarter.

body.text: SpaceX reported a profit of $4.4 billion for the three months through September, reversing a year-earlier loss, while revenue rose 161% to $14.6 billion, the Associated Press reported. The results exceeded analyst expectations.

The company’s artificial-intelligence business became its largest by revenue in the quarter, although Starlink remained its largest profit generator, according to AP. The earnings therefore reflect growth across both satellite connectivity and AI-related operations.

Musk said independent committees at SpaceX and Tesla had been formed to discuss a possible combination. He cautioned that a merger was not certain and that there were hurdles, and no transaction has been announced.

SpaceX reported $19.6 billion in capital expenditure in the quarter and forecast spending of $35 billion to $40 billion in the current quarter. The scale of planned investment and the status of any combination remain open questions for the companies and their investors.

stories.whyItMatters: The results make SpaceX’s AI and satellite businesses visible as distinct contributors to growth while showing a steep increase in planned investment. The potential Tesla combination remains exploratory, so the results do not resolve how the businesses might be financed or governed together.
stories.editorNote: Financial figures are attributed to AP coverage of company disclosures; the proposed combination is exploratory and unconfirmed.

stories.headline: Barclays to cut 5,000 jobs this year
stories.dek: The bank said technology including AI is part of an effort to reduce fixed costs; its finance chief said 1,000 cuts were already completed.
tldr: Barclays said it expects to cut around 5,000 jobs, or 5% of its workforce, during 2026 as it uses technology including AI to reduce fixed costs.
Chief financial officer Anna Cross said 1,000 cuts had already taken place and a further 4,000 were expected by the end of the fourth quarter.
The company described the move as part of its cost and returns program; the reports did not specify which roles or business units will account for the remaining cuts.

body.text: Barclays said it was cutting around 5,000 jobs this year, equivalent to 5% of its workforce, as it uses technology including AI to reduce fixed costs and improve returns. Reuters reported the announcement on October 22, and CNBC separately covered the planned cuts.
Chief financial officer Anna Cross told reporters that 1,000 reductions had already been completed. She said another 4,000 were expected by the end of the fourth quarter, according to Reuters.

The reports frame the reductions as part of Barclays’ effort to lower fixed costs through technology investment, including AI. They do not say that every eliminated position is being replaced by an AI system or identify the specific teams affected.

The announcement gives a scale and timetable for the planned reductions but leaves the distribution across roles and business units unspecified. The cited coverage also does not quantify how much of the total is directly attributable to AI rather than broader technology and cost measures.

stories.whyItMatters: The announcement is a concrete workforce figure attached to a bank’s technology-led cost program, while the company’s wording does not isolate AI as the cause of every cut. That distinction matters for interpreting claims about how AI investment is translating into employment changes.
stories.editorNote: Added in the 19:00 KST same-date merge. The headline follows Reuters wording; the article distinguishes Barclays’ stated technology rationale from the unquantified role of AI in the total.

stories.headline: Norway’s wealth fund posts $30 billion loss in third quarter
stories.dek: The $2.3 trillion sovereign fund reported a 0.5% negative return as higher interest rates weighed on fixed-income holdings.
tldr: Norway’s Government Pension Fund Global reported a third-quarter loss of 278 billion Norwegian crowns ($29.71 billion) and a return of minus 0.5%.
Deputy chief executive Trond Grande attributed weaker fixed-income results to rising interest rates, according to the fund’s statement cited by Reuters.
The reported quarterly result is a period-specific loss and does not by itself establish the fund’s longer-term performance.

body.text: Norway’s Government Pension Fund Global reported a third-quarter loss of 278 billion Norwegian crowns ($29.71 billion), with a minus 0.5% return on global investments. Reuters reported the result on October 22, and CNBC also covered the quarterly loss.
Deputy chief executive Trond Grande said the return was close to flat but slightly negative as rising interest rates weakened fixed-income investments, Reuters reported, citing the fund’s statement.

Reuters described the fund as worth about $2.3 trillion and the world’s largest sovereign wealth fund. It invests revenues from Norway’s oil and gas production across listed companies and other assets.
The result is a single-quarter measure and the cited reports do not treat it as a forecast. They also do not establish that the loss reflects a persistent change in the fund’s long-run performance.

stories.whyItMatters: The quarterly loss gives a current measure of how higher rates affected one of the world’s largest public investment pools, particularly its fixed-income holdings. Its scale makes the result relevant to global asset allocation, while the period-specific return should not be conflated with a long-term trend.
stories.editorNote: Added in the 19:00 KST same-date merge. Reuters provides the detailed result and quoted explanation; CNBC independently covered the loss.

stories.headline: World shares retreat as report of damage to oil tankers pushes oil prices higher
stories.dek: Brent crude rose after Iranian state television reported damage to seven tankers in the Strait of Hormuz; the vessel claims were not independently established in the cited reports.
tldr: Brent crude gained 3.2% to $112.27 per barrel as global shares and U.S. futures fell on October 22, according to the Associated Press.
Iranian state television reported that seven tankers were hit or damaged in the Strait of Hormuz, but AP attributed the account to Iranian media and did not independently confirm each incident.
Reuters and CNBC separately reported that Middle East tensions and attacks on Saudi infrastructure were adding to oil-market concerns.

body.text: Global shares and U.S. futures retreated on October 22 as oil prices rose following an Iranian state television report that seven tankers were hit or damaged in the Strait of Hormuz. The Associated Press said Brent crude gained 3.2% to $112.27 per barrel.

The vessel account came from Iranian state television, which said some tankers caught fire while others were damaged after hitting mines. AP’s report did not independently establish the reported damage to each vessel, so the count remains attributed to the Iranian account.

Reuters separately reported oil rising as Houthi attacks on Saudi targets heightened concern about a wider conflict and supply disruption. CNBC reported Brent above $112 amid Middle East tensions and reports that the U.S. and Israel were weighing possible strikes on Iran.

The reports describe a fast-moving geopolitical risk premium in energy markets, but the available accounts do not establish the tanker report’s full details or quantify any lasting supply loss. The intraday price move is a market snapshot rather than a forecast.

stories.whyItMatters: The Strait of Hormuz is a critical oil-shipping route, so reports of vessel damage can move energy prices and broader markets before the underlying facts are fully verified. The distinction between reported damage and confirmed supply loss is material to interpreting the price response.
stories.editorNote: Added in the 19:00 KST same-date merge. Tanker damage is explicitly attributed to Iranian state television; price figures retain their source-specific time context.
